name: Psychrometric
seoDesc: Psychrometric: work out partial vapour pressure (Pv) from the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb and the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp. A free physics…
summary: The Psychrometric calculator returns partial vapour pressure (Pv). The inputs are the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb, the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp, the wet bulb temperature and the temperature of moist, cooled air. It suits a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation. The panel waits for the button. Edit a field, press Calculate, and compare — one input at a time is enough to see what drives the answer.

sections.title: How does the Psychrometric calculator work?
sections.html:
The Psychrometric calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports partial vapour pressure (Pv) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb (Pₛ), the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp (Pw), the wet bulb temperature (Twb) and the temperature of moist, cooled air (Tc).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Psychrometric calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb, the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp and the wet bulb temperature — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Psychrometric calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns partial vapour pressure (Pv), derived from the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb, the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp and the wet bulb temperature. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Psychrometric calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the saturated vapour pressure at Tdb, the saturated pressure at wet bulb temp, the wet bulb temperature and the temperature of moist, cooled air, which is 7 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter altitude (Z) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Altitude (Z) opens in meters and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the Psychrometric calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
